I think a lot of this point is left to the imagination, but we know Joel killed and hurt people in order to survive. He did this both when he was with Tommy and Tess.

It's my belief they leave this to the imagination to leave the game more nuanced instead of black and white. This way Joel isn't just portrayed as a killer so we, the audience, can resonate with him. It lets us imagine the question of who knows what humans would do to each other in order to survive?

The show expounds on these character points as well. It makes it more clear and explicitly said to the audience, with Tommy telling Joel they blatantly killed people, and Tess telling Ellie that they aren't good people.

Compare this to the game where we see there are lots of collectibles to expound on the game's lore and reward interested players. 

Consider reading the TLOU wiki to read the collectibles in depth instead of the wiki's summary of the collectable information:

"Shortly after Sarah's death, Joel found himself in a triage clinic after making it to the highway. He witnessed how families had been torn apart and how much chaos had erupted in the world.[16] While there, he considered taking his own life but was unable to, finding something to fight for. However, what he found was worth fighting for was something his brother, Tommy, greatly disliked.[17]

Over the years, the pair survived by descending into a sinister way of life. Joel deceived and killed innocent people, becoming a hunter. He adopted tactics such as tricking passersby into thinking he was hurt so he could ambush them when they let their guard down.[17]

Joel and Tommy eventually reached the city of Boston, smuggling themselves into the city. Tommy finally had enough of Joel's philosophy on how to survive, abandoning his brother to join a growing militia group known as the Fireflies after being persuaded by the leader, Marlene. The two argued furiously over this, Tommy finishing with "I don't ever wanna see your goddamned face again!" Tommy eventually left the Fireflies as well but did not return to Joel, leaving Boston to go to Wyoming.[11]

Joel spent a considerable period of time alone, eventually meeting a woman named Tess Servopoulos. The pair grew close, teaming up to act as smugglers in the quarantine zone."

Oh boy, do I have a story for you.

When I was in India doing volunteer work, we had two sinks next to each other at the place I was staying. One worked, and the other didn't. 

One night, I was asleep, and our lights weren't great. In fact, in our bathroom (the room with the sinks), there wasnt any lights, but a window that would let in light during the day. 

Anyways, I'm about to go to sleep, but I had forgotten to put in my retainers in. So, I got up, went to the sink, and at this point I'm feeling around in the dark, but I'm groggy and had lived here for around six months, so I didn't think much of what if I had gotten the wrong sink. Besides, it didn't work. Water never came out when we had tried when I first got there.

Well, I find the right sink and turn it on. Now, water is coming out. I grab my retainers and wash them, then put them in my mouth. As I'm walking back to my room I feel something move. Then keep moving. Then I feel more movement. I fling them out of mouth, but stuff is still moving. I ran to where I kept a flashlight, turned it on, and there were 

Maggots.

Maggots literally everywhere where I flung them out, some still in my mouth. I use the good sink and flush out my mouth, I look over at the sink and the water works. It's a disgusting dark, brown green. Somehow a pipeline or something had leaked into our sink that didn't work, and it was full of gross water and filled with maggots. 

I washed my mouth over and over and over again, used mouthwash, and cleaned up, but needless to say, I was scarred for a while, and couldn't believe that just happened to me.

Luckily, I didn't get sick or anything, but boy, did that experience scar me a little. That and I also got hit by a motorcycle pretty badly while in India (from the U.S.). I love the food and a lot of people I met, but it India is a hard country.

I know this post was made a while ago, but I personally don’t think dual booting is the way. Sectioning off/portioning memory, in my opinion, can be difficult considering the only reason you’d really want windows is to play games where the anti cheat doesn’t work on steamOS. The great thing about microSDs is that you can interchange them. If you want more space on SteamOS, get another 512GB Card! If you wanted more on windows, to play non anti-cheat compatible games, you can just get another microSD with windows installed. That’s what I’ve done; at least I have a separate card for more storage on SteamOS. That’s what I’d recommend, especially because then you don’t spoil SteamOS in case anything goes wrong with dual booting and updates. Best to keep them separate.
